texts: mixed: the rule itself fires correctly — each Keeper who marries into a fisher family gets a keeping-the-station event tied to that marriage — but "marries into a fisher family" is recorded with a spatial destination role, as though the Keeper travelled to the family, instead of the plain "into" relation, which distorts the marriage-alliance sense. Giving the marriage an ordinary object removes the prepositional verb: "When a Keeper marries a member of a fisher family, that Keeper keeps the station."

good. the permission lands as a kind-level norm on keeper_child and "decline apprenticeship" is unpacked, so "what may they decline?" answers; note that the capitalized "Keeper" is read as an ordinary modifier fused into the kind symbol, so the parse itself carries no link back to the Keeper class.
